profile.headline: Electrical Engineer focusing on Firmware Development & Embedded Systems Design/Architecture
profile.summary:
I’m an embedded Electrical Engineer with over a decade of experience working on embedded software/firmware development for new product development as well as legacy hw support in a variety of industries including consumer electronics and defense. My firmware development (C/C++) and electrical engineering experience ranges from quick-turn prototypes to high volume, DFM products with cross-discipline teams (UI/UX, ME, EE, SWE). I have always thrived in the bare-metal embedded C space across many architectures and MCUs, as well as writing supporting test and configuration GUIs using the QT framework, bash scripting on Linux gateways and VMs, python when it’s the right tool for the job, and I have dabbled in front/backend web design. I consider myself a jack-of-all-trades, master of none, and will never admit to being an SME on any topic because there’s always more to learn. 

I enjoy working on and with teams who have no problem saying phrases like “I don’t know the answer, but I can find out”, and “I messed up, let’s figure out how to learn from this and move forward.” I’ve been called a “straight-shooter” and pride myself on WYSIWYG. I am collaborative by nature, and I believe engineering problems can be solved by getting the right people in the room in a work culture that promotes open communication without fear of messing up during the first attempt. Mistakes lead to growth. 

I also strive to incrementally improve engineering processes on every team I’m on, in a thoughtful way that manages “process overhead” to allow teams to move quickly while developing new products, but taking the time to document the design decisions and system details to allow us to build up and scale the project scope over time (modified Agile for firmware/hardware).

In my down time, I enjoy introducing young people to STEM by facilitating Girls Who Code after school programs, and coaching/mentoring FIRST org robotics teams (FLL and FRC). I also mentor college and high school design teams, and volunteer to promote STEM in local schools.

I love what I do, and I feel privileged to have found my dream career path in embedded systems and software engineering!
